title: Salvaging the Generic Standard-to-Ideal Reduction
summary: The classical first-step reduction gives a lower bound on an upper bound and cannot achieve optimal security in that role; it remains open whether it can be salvaged for useful, ideally optimal, security bounds.

formal_statement.body: For tweakable blockciphers, determine whether the generic standard-to-ideal reduction can be salvaged for standard-model security proofs so that it yields useful, ideally optimal, security bounds, despite the limitation that this classical first-step reduction gives a lower bound on an upper bound and therefore cannot achieve optimal security when used in that role.

scope.domain: Security reductions for tweakable blockciphers in standard-model cryptographic proofs.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether the generic standard-to-ideal reduction can be salvaged to yield useful, ideally optimal, security bounds for standard-model proofs.

citations.label: Insuperability of the Standard Versus Ideal Model Gap for Tweakable Blockcipher Security

progress.summary: The source presents this as an explicit question about salvaging the generic standard-to-ideal reduction. It notes that Theorem 4 gives a lower bound on an upper bound and that using this classical first step cannot yield optimal security.
citation_labels: Bart Mennink et al., Insuperability of the Standard Versus Ideal Model Gap for Tweakable Blockcipher Security
